full_judgment:
3. In Writ petition No. 2073 of 1995, the facts, in short are that the Petitioner ANM Balayet Hossain obtained his Master's Degree in Science from the University of Dhaka and joined the respondent No.1; Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Petrobangla) on 11-8-1976 as Assistant Geophysicist. On 1-7-1977 he was promoted to the post of Geophysicist, to be again promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-1983. On 1-7-1989 the Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration Company Limited (hereinafter called the BAPEX) was formed as a subsidiary Company of the Petrobangla. The petitioner's service with the respondent No. 1 continued to be governed by the Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. XXI of 1985). The petitioner and some other officers of the respondent No. 1 were sought to be permanently transferred to the constituted BAPEX by an order dated 22-11-1989. The said transfer order was challenged by one Fazlul Karim, the then President of the Petrobangla Officers’ Association by filing a writ petition being Writ Petition No.1921 of 1991. After hearing the High Court Division struck down the said transfer order with a declaration that the order so passed by the respondent No. 1 was without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect by the judgment dated 6-9-1994. Against the said judgment the respondent No. 1 preferred an appeal before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court being Civil Petition-for Leave to-Appeal No. 754 of 1994 and the Appellate Division dismissed the petition for leave to appeal and affirmed the judgment of the High Court Division by the judgment dated 11-12-1994. 

 4. In view of the affirmation of the judgment of the High Court Division by the Appellate Division the petitioners and other officers transferred en-bloc to the BAPEX by Order Nos. 21, 27, 70 dated 22-11-1989 are all officers of the Petrobangla. During pendency of the above mentioned writ petition the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah of the Petrobangla was promoted as Deputy General Manager by an order dated 11-2-1993 and the respondent No.12 Shamsul Haque to the post of Deputy General Manager by an order dated 24-3-1992. Both the respondent Nos. 5 and 12 are junior to the petitioner. The said orders of promotion were made ignoring the Service Rules and seniority of the petitioner and also without taking into consideration the petitioner's case for promotion. Likewise the respondent No. 1 in utter disregard of the judgment passed in Writ Petition No.1921 of 1991 promoted the respondents No. 6 to 11 to the posts of Deputy General Manager. The respondent Nos. 6 to 11 is officers of the Petrobangla and they all are junior to the petitioner. The petitioner and his other colleagues being affected by the aforesaid orders of promotion of the respondent Nos. 5 to 12 made representations to the respondent No.2, Chairman of the Petrobangla through proper channel for restoration of their seniority and for consideration of their cases for promotion. Having had no response to the first representation a second representation was made on 5-2-1995 but no positive result emerged from such representation. Instead of rectifying the illegal actions of the respondent No.1 an Office Order being No. 21.27.70(part)/541 dated 7-3-1995 was issued with certain modifications made in the order dated 22-11-1989 and making the transfer of the petitioner and others subject to conditions as spelt out in the said order dated 7-3-1995. The petitioner and his other colleagues objected to the said office order as being contrary to the Service Rules and the judgments of the superior Courts. The said order was also assailed by the officers of the Petrobangla but this objection did not yield any result. The Petrobangla authorities by their orders dated 5-1-1994 and 9-1-1994 defied matters relating to the determination of seniority for promotion in violation of Establishment Division Memo No.l/16/69/D-2 dated 31-12-1970. The principles laid down in the aforesaid Memorandum of the Establishment Division are being followed by the respondent No. 1 in the Service Rules/Regulations framed in the year 1988. As the orders of promotion affected by the impugned orders contained in Annexures-B and C series are violative of the principles of seniority and the Service Regulations of 1988 and the orders having the effect of supersession of this petitioner in service to the detriment of his career the same are without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. The petitioner had a notice of demand for justice issued upon the respondents No.1 to 4 but no reply thereto was received by the petitioner. So, the petitioner having no other efficacious remedy available to him moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. The respondent Nos. 1 and 3 by filing two separate Affidavits-in-opposition opposed the Rule. Both the respondents No.1 and 3 have denied the material averments made in the writ petition. It is asserted by the respondent No.1 that the writ petitioner having no legal right cannot maintain the writ petition. It is stated by the respondent No.1 that on 22-11-1989 the Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation decided to abolish the Directorate of Exploration of Petrobangla and create a new Company under the name and style of the Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration Company Limited (BAPEX). Due to the formation of the above mentioned Company the manpower of the Petrobangla was reduced to only 804 personnel. But, on the other hand, the newly constituted Company the BAPEX had augmented in size and manpower with 1363 officers and staff. The size of the BAPEX being larger compared to the Petrobangla, the prospects of promotion in the BAPEX became far more brighter than the Petrobangla. The officers in the Petrobangla were promoted when chances for promotion were available. The similar condition was also created in the newly constituted BAPEX, In compliance with the judgment of Writ Petition No.1921 of 1991 the separate positions of officers and staff of the Petrobangla and the BAPEX was done away with by an office order dated 7-3-1995. It is stated by the respondent No.1 that previously the order of promotion was resisted and this phenomenon became more acute in the BAPEX than in the Petrobangla. It is further asserted by the respondent No.1 that promotion to a higher post cannot be claimed as of right under Regulation 14 of the Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation Staff Service Regulations of 1988. There are specific and definite guide-lines for promotion. The respondent No. 1 denies that the petitioner's case was ignored when the question of his promotion came up for consideration by the respondent No. 1. The petitioner's prospect for promotion would be from Manager (Geophysics) to Senior Manager (Geophysics). The respondent No. 12 and the petitioner belonged to the same discipline, they being from Geophysical Cadre and while considering the case of promotion of the petitioner and the respondent No. 12 under Regulation 14(4) of the Regulations of 1988 a comparative assessment was made by the Promotion Committee and having noticed that the respondent No.12 secured 84.42 marks as against 70.26 marks secured by the petitioner out of total 100 marks, the case of the respondent No. 12 became more weighty marks-wise than the petitioner and so the former was given promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager. In the case of promotion of the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah he was promoted to the post of Deputy General Manager in consideration of his tact and aptitude shown by him in the Administration Division of the Petrobangla. The respondent No. 5 did not take his promotion from the Geophysical Cadre and as such there is no reason of the petitioner's being prejudiced by such promotion of the respondent No. 5. After the issue of the office order dated 7-3-1995 a necessity was felt for its revision and so came the office order dated 23-11-1995. It is stated by the respondent No.1 that the principles of seniority as laid down in the Memo dated 31-12-1970 are not applicable to the officers and staff of the respondent No. 1 except what were accepted in the Regulations of 1988. For promotion to the grade of Taka 3700-4825 merit was given preference over seniority and in exceptional cases provisions have been made for promotion out of turn. The promotions of the respondent Nos. 6 to 11 to the posts of Deputy General Manager have been made keeping in view their respective ratings which are as shown below: 

 6. The petitioner previously was considered thrice for promotion but his assessment being far below the desired level he was not considered for promotion as Deputy General Manager (Geophysics) as per the service regulations. The High Powered Selection Committee drawn from the Petrobangla and the BAPEX considered the cases of promotion of each individual officer and there was no scope for making promotions illegally which the petitioner has called in question by filing this writ petition. 

 10. In Writ Petition No. 2084 of 1995 the case of the petitioner Azizun Nahar is that, after securing her Master’s Degree in Science from the University of Dhaka she joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Geologist on 26-7-1980. She was promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 1-7-1989. She has asserted that she is senior to the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr.Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 Md. Mozammel Huq and respondent No.9 Md Imaduddin who have been promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-1993 and Annexure-C series dated 14-1-1995. While giving the background of her case, she, it appears, has relied upon the facts as narrated in Wit Petition No. 2073 of 1995. It is stated by her that the respondent No.1 violating the principle of merit-cum-seniority gave promotion to the respondents Nos. 5 to 9. The order for promotion has been without lawful authority and, as such, they are of no legal effect. 

 It is stated by the respondent No.1 that after a comparative assessment of the marks secured by the petitioner and the above named respondents, it will be seen that she did not come up to the level of the above named respondents and so, she was not promoted. It is stated by the respondent No 1 that promotion cannot be claimed as of right and the Petrobangla authority did not commit any illegality in promoting the respondent Nos. 5 to 9 to the posts of Deputy General Manager. The writ petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable as she has no legal right with regard to promotion and as such, the Rule obtained by the petitioner is liable to be discharged. 

 13. In Writ Petition No. 2085 of 1995 the petitioner Syed Shamsul Alam has called in question the orders promoting the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 ARM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 10 Md Mozemmel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md Imaduddin to the posts of Deputy General Manager vide Annexures- B dated 11-2-93 and C series dated 14-1-95. The petitioner is a Master's Degree holder in Science from the University of Dhaka. First he was appointed by the respondent No. 1 on 12-1-1976 as Electronics Officer and subsequently he was promoted as Manager with effect from 28-11-1984. This petitioner while making out a case in his writ petition has narrated facts which tally with the facts narrated by the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2073 of 1995. His case is that in the matter of promotion to the post of Deputy General Manager, the respondent No. 1 illegally promoted respondent No. 5 to 11 who are his junior. By giving such promotions the respondent No. 1 has committed illegality and the impugned orders are without any lawful authority and, as such, not sustainable in law. 

 15. In Writ Petition No.2086 of 1995 the petitioner is M Yusuf Haroon. He obtained his Bachelor of Science Degree in Engineering (Civil) and joined the Petrobangla on 7-2-1979 as Assistant Engineer and he was promoted to the post of Manager/Deputy Chief Engineer with effect from 1- 7-1989. Respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No.10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md. Imaduddin who are junior to the petitioner have been most illegally promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C series dated 14-1-95. The impugned orders of promotion have been made without lawful authority and as such, they are liable to be struck down. 

 17. In Writ Petition No. 2087 of 1995 the petitioner is Md Abdur Razzaque, a Master of Science Degree holder from the University of Rajshahi who joined the service in the respondent No.1 as Assistant Geophysicist on 1-1-1981. He was thereafter promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 1-7-1989. He has called in question the orders of promotion given to the respondent No. 5 Dr. Ismat Mirza and respondent No. 6 A. Aziz Khan vide Annexure-B and B(1) dated 14-1-1995. It is stated by him that he is senior to both of the above named respondents. Facts narrated by the petitioner are identical with those of the Writ Petition No. 2073 of 1995. 

 18. The respondent Nos. 1 and 3 have entered appearance and opposed the Rule obtained by the petitioner on the facts that were set up by them and submitted in the above mentioned writ petition. It has been stated by the respondent No.1 that the petitioner has secured 77.55 marks out of 100 but respondent Nos. 5 and 6 secured 78.50 and 80.43 marks respectively out of 100 marks. Considering the low score of the petitioner his case for promotion was not considered and instead respondent Nos. 5 and 6 were promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager. 

 19. The petitioner Nazim Uddin Ahmed by filing Writ Petition No.2088 of 1995 has challenged the orders of promotion issued by Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C series dated 14-1-95. The petitioner has stated that he obtained his Master's Degree in Science from the University of Dhaka and joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Geologist on 24-6-80 and on 1-7-89 he was promoted to the post of Manager. The respondents Nos. 5 to l0 are junior to him and the respondent No.1 promoted them to the posts of Deputy General Manager without considering the case of the petitioner for promotion. The impugned orders having been passed without lawful authority, they are not legally sustainable. 

 21. In Writ Petition No.2089 of 1995 the petitioner is one Manzur Ahmed. He is a holder of Master of Science Degree from the University of Rajshahi and he joined Petrobangla as Assistant Chemist on 29-12-80. He was promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 1-7-89. This petitioner by filing this writ petition has questioned the legality of the orders as contained in Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C and C(1) dated 14-1-95 promoting the respondent No.5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No.7 AAziz Khan, respondent No. 8 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No.9 Md Imasuddin. It is stated by the petitioner that the respondents Nos. 5 to 9 are junior to him and without considering his case for promotion the above named respondents have been promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 in violation of the general principles of seniority and Regulation 14(4) of the Service Regulations of 1988. The impugned orders having been passed without lawful authority, they are not sustainable in law. 

 23. Md Abdul Baqi is the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2090 of 1995. He is a Master of Science Degree holder from the University of Dhaka and joined the service of the respondent No.1 on 24-6- 80 as Assistant Geologist. He was promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 1-7-1989. He by filing this writ petition has challenged the orders of promotion of the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 9 Md Mozammel Huq and respondents No. 10 Md Imaduddin vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) dated 14-1-95. It is contended by the petitioner that the above named respondents are junior to him but in the matter of promotion his case was not considered by the respondent No. 1 and the result was the promotion of the aforesaid respondents to the posts of Deputy General Manager. The impugned orders have been passed without lawful authority and, as such, they are not sustainable in law. 

 25. In Writ Petition No. 2091 of 1995 Nazma Begum is the petitioner. She is a Master of Science Degree holder from the University of Dhaka and she joined her service in the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Geologist on 19-9-1980. She got her promotion as Manager on 1-7-1989. She is senior to respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No.8 Md. Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 9 Md. Imaduddin who have been illegally promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexure-C, C(1) and C(2) dated 14-1-1995. The impugned orders are ex-facie illegal and, as such they are not sustainable in law. 

 27. The petitioner Md Mamunur Rashid of Writ Petition No. 2092 of 1995 has called in question the impugned orders as contained in Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C, C(l) and C(2) dated 14-1-95 by which the respondent No. 1 has promoted the respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md Imaduddin. The petitioner has stated that he is a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Dhaka. He joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Engineer on 18-6-80. He was promoted to the post of Manager/Deputy Chief Engineer with effect from 1-7 -89. He making a common cause with the petitioner of Writ Petition No. 2073 of 1995 has stated that the respondents Nos. 5 to 11 whom the respondent No.1 promoted as Deputy General Managers are junior to him. The impugned orders are palpably illegal for which they are not sustainable in law. 

 29. Md Nurul Islam, petitioner of writ petition No. 2093 of 1995 has challenged the impugned orders as contained in Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) dated 14-1-1995 by which the respondent No. 1 have given promotion to respondent No.5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6, Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No.9 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md Imaduddin to the posts of Deputy General Manager in the Petrobangla. The petitioner has stated that he is a Master of Science Degree holder from the University of Rajshahi and he joined the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Electronics on 7-1-1976. He was promoted as Manager with effect from 28-11-1984. The respondents No. 5 to 11 are junior to him but the respondent No. 1 disregarding the general principles of seniority and Service Regulations framed for regulation of the service of Officers and Employees of the Petrobangla and its subsidiary companies have made such promotions which being palpably illegal are not sustainable in law. 

 31. Md Azizur Rahman, petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2094 of 1995 by filing this writ petition has called in question the impugned orders as contained in Annexue-B and B(1) dated 11-2-93 and 6-9-94 respectively together with Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) all dated 14-1-95. By the aforesaid Annexures the respondent No. 1 has promoted respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Shahidul Islam, respondent No. 7 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 8 A Aziz Khan, respondent No.9 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 10 ARM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 11 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No.12 Md Imaduddin to the posts of Deputy General Manager. It is stated by the petitioner that after obtaining Diploma in Engineering from the Bangladesh Technical Education Board, Dhaka he joined the service of the respondent No. 1 on 13-6-70 as Trainee Driller and subsequently he got promotion to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-83. It is asserted by the petitioner that the respondents Nos. 5 to 12 who are all his junior in the service have been promoted in violation of the general principles of seniority and provisions of Regulation 14(4) of the concerned Service Regulations of 1988. The impugned orders having been made without lawful authority the same are not sustainable in law. 

 33. Md Abdul Jalil is the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2095 of 1995. He is a Master of Science Degree holder from the University of Rajshahi and he joined the respondent No. 1 on 3-11-78 as Assistant Geophysicist. He got his promotion to the post of Manager on 1-7-89. It is stated by the petitioner that respondent No.5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Fiki Hasan Hilmi, respondent No. 7 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 8 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 9 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 10 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 11 Md. Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 12 Md. Imaduddin who are all junior to the petitioner in service has been illegally promoted by the respondent No. 1 to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the impugned orders as contained in Annexures-B, B(1),C, C(1) and C(2) dated 11-2-93, 26-12-93 and 14-1-95 respectively. The aforesaid orders of promotion have been made by the respondent No. 1 in utter violation of the general principles of seniority and the provisions of Regulation 14(4) of the Regulations of 1988. That being the position the impugned orders are not legally sustainable. 

 35. In Writ Petition No. 2096 of 1995 the petitioner is Md Akkas Ali who after obtaining his Master’s Degree in Science from the University of Dhaka joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Geologist on 4-8-80. The last promotion he got to the post of Manager is on 1-7-1989. It is stated by him that respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 9 Md Imaduddin who are junior to the petitioner in service have been most illegally promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 by Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) all dated 14-1-1995. It is asserted by the petitioner that the impugned orders of promotion have been made without any lawful authority and, as such, they are not legally sustainable. 

 37. Ahmed Hossain is the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2097 of 1995. He is a Master of ScienceDegree holder from the University of Dhaka and he joined the service of the respondent No. 1 on 28.9.1977 as Geophysicist He was lastly promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-1983. It is stated by him that respondent No. 5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 AHM-Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md. Imaduddin have been illegally promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) all dated 14-1-95. The orders of promotion having been made in derogation of the general principles of Seniority and Service Regulations of 1988, the same are not legally sustainable. 

 39. In Writ Petition No. 2098 of 1995 Md. Rectwanul Huq is the petitioner. He is a Diploma Engineer and he joined his service in the respondent No. 1 on 13-6-1970 as Trainee Driller and he subsequently was promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-1983. He is senior to respondent No. 5 Md. Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Shahidul Islam, respondent No. 7 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 8 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 9 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 10 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 11 Md. Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 12 Md. Imaduddin but the respondent No. 1 disregarding the general principles of seniority and the provisions of the Service Regulations of 1988 promoted the above named respondents to the posts of Deputy General Manager vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-93 and B(1) dated 6-9-94 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) all dated 14-1-95. The aforesaid orders of promotion having been made without any lawful authority they are not sustainable in law. 

 41. Bayezid Ahmed is the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2099 of 1995. He is a Master’s Degree holder in Science from the University of Dhaka and he joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Geophysicist on 30-9-1977. He was lastly promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-1983. The respondent No.5 Md. Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 AHM Ali Ashraf, respondent No. 10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md Imaduddin arc all junior to him in service but the respondent No. 1 in utter disregard of the general principles of seniority and the Service Regulations of 1988 promoted the above named respondents to the posts of Deputy General Manager vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-1993 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) all dated 14-1-95. The impugned orders of promotion have been made without any lawful authority and, as such, they are not sustainable in law. 

 43. Shariful Islam Khandaker is the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 2100 of 1995. He is a. holder of Master of Science Degree from the University of Dhaka. After joining his service in the respondent No. 1 on 28-9-1977 as Geophysicist, he was lastly promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 31-12-1983. The respondent No.5 Md Mohiuddin Miah, respondent No. 6 Dr. Ismat Mirza, respondent No. 7 A Aziz Khan, respondent No. 8 AKM Shafiqur Rahman, respondent No. 9 AHM Ali Ashraf respondent No. 10 Md Mozammel Huq and respondent No. 11 Md Imaduddin who are all junior to the petitioner in service have been most illegally promoted to the posts of Deputy General Manager by the respondent No. 1 vide Annexure-B dated 11-2-1993 and Annexures-C, C(1) and C(2) dated 14-1-95. The impugned orders of promotion have been made without any lawful authority and, as such, the same are not sustainable in law. 

 45. In Writ Petition No. 2101 of 1995 Md Nurul Haque is the petitioner. After obtaining his Master's Degree in Science from the University of Dhaka the petitioner joined the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Geophysicist on 1-1-1981 and he was lastly promoted to the post of Manager with effect from 1-7-1989. It is stated-by him that respondent No. 5 Dr. Ismat Mirza and respondent No. 6 A Aziz Khan are junior to him in service but the respondent No. 1 disregarding the general principles of seniority and Service Regulations of 1988 promoted the respondents No. 5 and 6 to the posts of Deputy General Manager vide Annexure B and B(1) dated 14-1-1995. The impugned orders of promotion so made are ex facie illegal having not been made in accordance with law, they are not legally sustainable. 

 47. In Writ Petition No. 2267 of 1995 the petitioner Md Nasir Uddin Sarker has called in question the orders of promotion as contained in Annexures-B dated 26-12-94, B(1) dated 25-3-92, B(2) dated 25-3-92, B(3) dated 2-12-92 and B(4) dated 6-9-94. By the aforesaid impugned orders of promotion made by the respondent No. 1 promoting respondent No. 5 Md Mizanur Rahman, respondent No. 6 Nizam Shariful Islam, respondent No. 7 Golam Sarwar, respondent No. 8 Shafiullah Bhuiyan, respondent No. 9 Mridul Kanti Dey, respondent No. 10 Md Mahbubur Rahman, respondent No. 11 AM Saifuzzaman, respondent No. 12 Nirmal Kanti Bairagee and respondent No. 13 MA Mannan to the pasts of Manager, it is stated by the petitioner that after obtaining his Diploma in Electronics Engineering from the Chittagong Polytechnic Institute he joined the service of the respondent No. 1 as Assistant Engineer on 31-12-1980. On 30-4-1986 he was promoted to the post of Engineer. It is further stated by the petitioner that the respondents No. 5 to 13 are all junior to the petitioner but the respondent No. 1 promoted them to the posts of Manager in violation of the general principles of seniority and the Service Regulations of 1988. The impugned orders of promotion have been made by the respondent No. 1 without any lawful authority and, as such, they are not sustainable in law.
